title: AquaScope Bench Phase 2 reference plans: expert plans for hydrology agents at real sites (25 cases)
description: Twenty-five reference plans for the plan-quality benchmark of hydrology agents (AquaScope Bench Phase 2, AquaScope issue #367). Each case is a client's brief at a real site drawn from the AquaScope station catalog (gauges of the U.S. Geological Survey, the Environment Agency of England and Hub'Eau, and bare points), the method-selection playbook it maps to with the intake the brief fixes, a snapshot of the data reconnaissance at that place (the catalog stations within 50 km with their record spans, the BasinATLAS catchment attributes, the donor count, the method-sufficiency table of the AquaScope registry), and the plan a hydrologist would write for it: the ordered steps with their tool, registry method and gates, the optional steps, the tools and methods not defensible at that site, or a decline with its kind when the data or the brief cannot carry the question. The cases cover flood risk, ungauged flow, groundwater decline, drought status, supply reliability, irrigation feasibility and water quality; seven decline; three are off-tree briefs no single playbook branch covers (an at-site flood fit compared with a regional estimate, a supply question whose demand is a crop's, a drought question that names the well and the river). A plan is scored by the coverage of the reference's tools, methods and gates, the absence of forbidden methods and the absence of extraneous steps, with a documented formula in aquascope.gym.plans. The README describes the format, the scoring, the sites and the licences of the underlying catalogs. Results of the first runs (the playbook tree, the AquaScope Studio Methodologist on Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Haiku 4.5) are in the AquaScope repository under aquascope/gym/results/2026-09-07/.
notes: Written with aquascope (https://github.com/Rekin226/aquascope), issue #367 (AquaScope Bench Phase 2, formerly HydroGym, epic #363). Recon snapshots carry catalog-level station metadata (identifiers, names, positions, record spans) from USGS (public domain), Environment Agency (OGL-UK-3.0) and Hub'Eau / Eaufrance (Licence Ouverte / Etalab 2.0), and catchment attributes from BasinATLAS, HydroATLAS v1.0 (CC BY 4.0, Linke et al. 2019). No observation record is included.
